Leaker Claims Intel is Reportedly Preparing a 12 P-Core Razor Lake-S Design, With Up To 120 MB of bLLC Cache Alongside 28-Core SKU
Things are getting interesting when it comes to the Nova Lake successor. Despite Nova Lake-S being the first-ever family to feature Big Last Level Cache, or bLLC, Intel is reportedly carrying it to the Razor Lake-S family as well. We have already reported on the possible configuration for the Nova Lake-S alongside the bLLC cache size recently, and now we have some crucial info for some of the Razor Lake-S SKUs as well.
Prominent leaker @Jaykihn0 is claiming that Intel is preparing different variants of Razor Lake-S chips, including chips with E cores and P-Core-only variants. According to the latest claim, the Razor Lake-S could feature a 28-core design as well as a 16-core CPU, featuring 8+16+4 and 12+0+4 core configuration variants. Both are supposedly the bLLC variants, featuring up to 144 MB of bLLC cache.
However, the 12-P-Core-only variant will reportedly feature a 120 MB bLLC cache instead of 144 MB. This is the same cache size as we recently reported for the Intel Core Ultra 9 4900, which is a 6+12+4 Nova Lake-S variant with a 65W rating. However, the 12 P-Core Razor Lake-S reportedly doesn't have any E-cores, which is interesting, as it targets a different performance segment rather than simply being another variation of Intel's conventional hybrid layout.
Intel's bLLC is expected to serve as the company's answer to AMD's 3D V-Cache technology, which helps immensely in improving gaming performance. We already know that Nova Lake-S bLLC variants aim to deliver such a gaming performance boost, and according to the recent leaks, some chips could deliver up to 20% better gaming performance than Arrow Lake-S.
